is_anopheles.evidence: The study tests larvae of Anopheles gambiae (Ladji strain) from Benin (page 2, 'Quantification of larvicidal activities of PP on Anopheles Ladji').

reports_target_markers.evidence: No insecticide-resistance markers were genotyped in this study. The authors only cite prior literature regarding the kdr mutation status of the Ladji strain: 'The kdr mutation, which is one of the mechanisms conferring the resistant status to this strain appears to be homozygous in this mosquito population, with an allelic frequency of one [13]' (page 2).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype assays were performed and no genotype or allele counts are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Larvae of Anopheles gambiae were collected from the traditional community of Ladji, near Cotonou, Republic of Benin (page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study testing the larvicidal efficacy of petroleum products.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The exact collection dates/years of the mosquito larvae tested are not specified in the manuscript.

supplement.evidence: No supplementary materials cited containing relevant genotype data.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the larvicidal efficacy and mode of action of various petroleum products (petrol, kerosene, engine oil, waste oil) against larvae of a pyrethroid-resistant strain of Anopheles gambiae from Ladji, Benin. No genetic marker assays or genotyping data were generated.
exclusion_reasons: No target insecticide resistance markers were genotyped (the paper only cites previous literature for the kdr status of the strain).
No extractable genotype or allele frequency data reported.
